summary_paragraph: A female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted with fever and right mandibular pain four days after a tooth extraction. She developed a fever post-dialysis and was found to have inflammatory changes in the right buccal and masticator spaces on CT, consistent with a soft tissue infection without abscess. She was initially treated with vancomycin, then transitioned to Unasyn and later discharged on oral Augmentin. Her fever resolved, and pain improved. During admission, she was noted to have mild transaminitis, likely due to simvastatin, which was held. She underwent scheduled hemodialysis, remained stable, and was discharged home in good condition with instructions to complete antibiotics, avoid alcohol and Tylenol, and follow up on liver tests.
problems: Other and unspecified diseases of the oral soft tissues
Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
